decisions.reason: As a consumer superfood drink mix far from a German chemical producer’s core business and only lightly signaled on the website, it carries weak strategic fit and limited public commitment, so management is comparatively willing to cut it despite launch investment.

Modular waste-to-energy plant extensions fit the firm’s industrial capabilities and, even if early traction is uncertain, sunk development costs and a plausible temporary market ramp-up favor continuing.

The waste-oil-to-energy plant appears most visibly committed because it had its own webpage, and escalation of commitment makes management especially likely to persist with such a publicly backed core-adjacent offering.

Plastic-waste-to-fuel technology is strategically close to process and chemical know-how, so management is likely to justify the initial investment and attribute any early weakness to normal commercialization delays rather than exit quickly.
